goal.problem: Scribe stores all notes in a single flat JSONL file that grows ~5KB/session, risks line-level corruption on concurrent writes, and forces full-file parsing for every operation -- none of which scales past a few months of active use.
goal.solution: Replace the monolithic JSONL with a folder-per-type layout where each note is an individual file, metadata lives in per-folder index files, and archival moves old entries to subfolders.
goal.value: Claude sessions start faster (index-only reads), note corruption is isolated to single files, the store is human-browsable, and the architecture supports future scaling (search, multi-user, cloud sync).

components.name: Type folders
components.description: One directory per note type (todos/, handoffs/, decisions/, wishlists/, blockers/, context/, general/), each containing an index.jsonl, individual .md note files, and an archive/ subfolder.

components.name: Learnings folder
components.description: learnings/ directory with same structure (index.jsonl + individual files + archive/) but manual-only archival -- no auto-archive process.

components.name: General folder
components.description: general/ directory as catch-all for notes without a specific type. Same structure as other type folders.

components.name: Global counter
components.description: next_id file at .apiary/scribe/next_id holding a single integer, shared across all types. Read-increment-write on each add operation.

components.name: Index files
components.description: Per-folder index.jsonl containing metadata records: id, status, session, timestamp, summary. Source of truth for all metadata; note .md files hold only content.

components.name: Backup system
components.description: backups/ directory for daily snapshots of all index files. Script only -- cron scheduling is deferred.

components.name: Migration script
components.description: scripts/migrate_scribe_v2.py -- one-way migration from current JSONL layout (notes.jsonl, notes_archive.jsonl, learnings.jsonl) to new folder structure. Old files preserved as backup.

components.name: Repair subcommand
components.description: notes.py repair -- rebuilds indexes from existing .md files, recovers from corruption, regenerates next_id from max observed ID.

shape.integration_point: scribe/notes.py CLI (all existing commands preserved), core/startup.py (startup injection reads indexes instead of full JSONL).
shape.pattern: Follows the existing memory/ pattern (individual files per entry) but adds index files for fast listing.
shape.data_flow: CLI command -> resolve type folder -> read/write index.jsonl + individual .md file -> return result. Startup: glob type folders -> read each index.jsonl -> merge + format -> inject into prompt.
shape.dependencies: Existing .apiary/scribe/ directory layout, core/utils/filelock.py for index writes.

behavior.input: Same CLI interface as today -- notes.py add --type todo --content "...", notes.py get 306, notes.py list, etc.
behavior.processing: 1. On add: read next_id, increment, write new index entry to <type>/index.jsonl, write content to <type>/<id>.md, update next_id. 2. On get: scan all type index.jsonl files for matching ID (or accept type hint for O(1) lookup), read the corresponding .md file, print summary + body. 3. On list: read index.jsonl from specified type folder (or merge all if no --type), sort by timestamp, print summaries. 4. On done: update status in the type's index.jsonl. 5. On archive (auto, 30-day): move index entry from <type>/index.jsonl to <type>/archive/index.jsonl, move .md file to <type>/archive/<id>.md. 6. On search (--search): substring match against summary field in index files only. 7. On startup injection: read all active index files, format summaries, read latest handoff .md file only. 8. On backup (daily cron): copy all index.jsonl files to backups/<date>_<type>.jsonl.
behavior.output: Same CLI output format as today. list shows summaries, get shows full content, get --full preserved for compatibility.

error_cases.trigger: Missing index file for a type folder

error_cases.behavior: Skip entry, log warning, suggest notes.py repair.
Scan all indexes for max ID, recreate counter, log warning.

edge_cases.condition: get <id> when ID exists in archive
edge_cases.behavior: Search archive indexes, print with [archived] indicator.
Merge all type indexes, sort by timestamp.
No limit enforced, file handles any size.

edge_cases.condition: Concurrent writes to same type index
edge_cases.behavior: FileLock on the index file ensures atomicity.

in_scope: Folder-per-type layout with individual note files
Archive-to-subfolder for all note types (auto for notes, manual for learnings)
Startup injection rewrite to use indexes
One-way migration script from current JSONL layout
Daily index backup mechanism (script only, cron setup deferred)
New general type for untyped notes
repair subcommand to rebuild indexes from files + recover from corruption
out_of_scope: Cron job setup for backups -- script exists, scheduling is separate
Full-text search across note bodies -- index summary search is sufficient for now
Multi-user collaboration (#167) -- depends on this layout but is a separate effort
Scribe cleaner/consolidation agent (#9) -- operates on top of this layout, separate effort
Learnings auto-archive process -- folder exists, process deferred
Changes to memory/ layout -- already works, untouched
must_not_break: All existing CLI commands (add, get, list, done, update, archive, learn, learnings, unlearn, show, handoff-sessions)
Startup injection in core/startup.py (must produce equivalent output)
Backfill agent ability to write handoff notes
Budgeter hooks that read session IDs from notes

acceptance_criteria: Given an empty .apiary/scribe/ dir, when notes.py add --type todo --content 'test' is run, then a todos/ folder exists with index.jsonl containing one entry and 1.md containing 'test'
Given notes of multiple types exist, when notes.py list is run without --type, then all types are shown merged and sorted by timestamp
Given a note with ID 306, when notes.py get 306 is run, then the summary from the index and the body from <type>/306.md are printed
Given a note older than 30 days, when the archive process runs, then the index entry moves to <type>/archive/index.jsonl and the .md file moves to <type>/archive/
Given a corrupted index (malformed JSON line), when notes.py list is run, then the corrupted entry is skipped with a warning and all other entries are shown
Given a missing .md file referenced by an index entry, when notes.py get <id> is run, then [content missing] is printed with a repair suggestion
Given the old JSONL layout exists, when migrate_scribe_v2.py is run, then all notes are split into type folders with correct index entries and individual files, and old files are preserved as backup
Given the migration has run, when notes.py list --type todo is run against the new layout, then output matches the pre-migration output
Given next_id is missing, when notes.py add is run, then the counter is rebuilt from existing indexes and the new note gets the correct next ID
Given a note is archived, when notes.py get <id> is run, then the archived note is found and displayed with an [archived] indicator
Given startup injection runs, when a session starts, then only index summaries are injected (not full note bodies) and only the latest handoff file is read
Given the backup script runs, when backups/ is checked, then it contains dated copies of all current index files
Given two concurrent add operations to the same type, when both complete, then both entries exist in the index with unique IDs and no corruption
